author: Codex documentation author; corrections by DOC-029 source-review author agent (documents)

prerequisites: Signed-in fictional role in its own browser context on the work documentation lab.

Walkthrough-created Contracts, Matters and Entities named "DOC-029 documents ...", with Jonas Weber on the Contract team; reviewer-built fixtures in docs/documentation/batches/DOC-029/documents/fixtures.
Comment attachments posted through the API as fixture setup; named browser-network fixtures for the refused upload.
scenarios.expected: A logical Document retains its linear Version chain and the paper's ownership/provenance is visible. Unsupported corrections, failed uploads, and insufficient access do not silently alter a Version or its provenance.
scenarios.actual: 14 recorded browser steps passed for this role. Upload with one file created a v1 Document named from its filename; Kind offered the six hand-set kinds and no Generated redline; several files opened the bulk import dialog. Edit details renamed the Document without touching the chain. Add version raised it to v2 and the expanded v1 opened as version 1 and downloaded its original bytes with note, kind and uploader kept. The same file uploaded again made a separate chain. The Kind correction changed the kind only. Mark as executed copy pinned v1, a v3 upload left the pin on v1, and Unmark cleared it. Make primary moved the Primary mark. A Matter had no Kind control, Kind column, Make primary or executed-copy item, and an Entity row had no Primary mark or designation items. An archived Contract had no Upload and refused a direct upload with 409 until restored. A refused Version upload showed its message and left the chain unchanged. A Legal only attachment filed as a Confidential New Document with the switch preselected, a preview's File to Contract appended a New Version with its note, and a Matter attachment filed through File to Matter with no Kind and the switch label "Confidential — restrict to the contract team".

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the article author and the source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.
API calls created fictional records, comment attachments and team membership as fixture setup and read results back; the credited actions used the browser controls the article names.
The refused upload used a browser-network fixture answering 413; the deployment's real upload limit was not reached.
Generated redline was confirmed absent from Upload and Kind correction choices; a Comparison export was not created, so correcting a Generated redline Version was not attempted.

Business User Portal claims (Add version on the Primary Document, no designation, kind, folder, archive, delete or filing controls, 403 for each attempt) are recorded as supplementary business_user steps in the same log; V-C26 does not require that role.

The shared work lab was used by other agents at the same time; only records named DOC-029 documents ... were created. One Administrator record page showed "Something went wrong." once during an earlier run and loaded after Reload; the final run recorded no such error.

compatibilityReview.summary: I inspected the app diff from 3fa407e3 to 57e77e38 and found no change to Document, Version, folder, preview, repository, archive or delete behavior or labels; the only Document-surface change is the archived uploader color. I replayed the round 1 documents walkthrough on the work2 lab built from 57e77e38, and all 117 steps passed for Administrator, Legal Team Member and Business User.
